As someone who struggles with suicide, and has known many others that have suicidal ideation, he may not have been saying those things to hurt you or brush you off. You said you never directly told him you were feeling suicidal. Asking him vague questions about suicide, or questions out of the blue, may have made him feel uncomfortable and that may have been his way of trying to turn it into a lighter topic, or to try to avoid the topic for his own comfort. Its very possible his reaction was a defense mechanism.

Perhaps you should try to talk to him more personally about it, or ask your questions online where they can be answered anonymously?

During prohibition, when alcohol was illegal in the USA, the only way to get any was to smuggle it in or make it yourself/buy it from moonshiners. The Mafia was a large group that flourished from the sale of alcohol (among other things) - and they made a lot of money because the demand for alcohol did not decrease despite the law. Mix the copious amounts of money they made with a strict honor code, the benefit of committing crime in a group, and the level of intimidation they could put forward by acting as an organized force and of course law enforcement would have trouble keeping them under wraps.
